- [ASSISTANT_SAID] JavaScript is a high-level, object-oriented programming language used primarily for client-side web development.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] JavaScript allows developers to create interactive web pages and web applications by manipulating the Document Object Model (DOM).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] JavaScript syntax is similar to other C-style programming languages, with variables, functions, loops, and conditionals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] JavaScript can be run in any modern web browser and is also used in many popular web frameworks such as React, Angular, and Vue.js.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] ReactJS is a JavaScript library used for building user interfaces or UI components, developed by Facebook.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] React allows developers to build reusable UI components that can be easily rendered and updated based on changes to application state.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] React utilizes a virtual DOM to efficiently update the UI without reloading the entire page.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] React provides a declarative approach to building UI components, allowing developers to define what should be displayed based on the current state of the application.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] React includes features such as lifecycle methods and the ability to manage state and props.
